correctness.rationale: A uniform recursive tree is constructed with independent uniform earlier-parent choices. For fixed birth indices 2<=i<j<=n, the event that i has unique child j and no other descendants has exactly (i-1)(n-3)! parent sequences among (n-1)!, giving probability (i-1)/((n-1)(n-2)). Deleting the pair yields a uniform independent (n-2)-vertex recursive tree and a uniform earlier parent A among its first i-1 labels, with depth-sum law P_n|E_{i,j} =_d P_{n-2}+2D_A+3 independent of j. Summing over j gives the probability (i-1)(n-i)/((n-1)(n-2)), conditional mean and covariance with total path length exactly factor times [2(H_{i-1}-H_{n-2})+(n-2)/(n-1)]. The bracket increases by 2/i and crosses from negative at i=2 to positive at i=n-1 for n>=4; harmonic asymptotics yield alpha(1-alpha)(1+2log alpha) with root exp(-1/2). Independent exhaustive rational enumeration for n=3,...,8 corroborates all indexed covariances; only the deletion coupling proves arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: Holmgren and Janson (2014) Theorems 1.4 and 1.15 describe aggregate fringe-subtree counts and their covariances, not a fixed birth-index two-vertex indicator paired with total root-path length. Feng et al. (2008) also study aggregate subtree-size phases; Fuchs/Hwang/Neininger address profiles. Resultary publication on forcing root attachment versus total path length concerns a different event and no two-vertex fringe deletion law. An aggregate covariance cannot recover opposing age-indexed contributions, so the additional exact conditional distribution and single sign switch are not merely rephrased. Specialist marked-fringe mixed moments might nevertheless predate this result.
